episode_title: $100 Oil, $6 Corn, and Cuts to Farm Subsidies with Steve Bruere & Dave Muth

real_qa.q: What is the correlation between global crude oil prices above $100 per barrel and corn prices at $6 or higher?
real_qa.r: Going back to the beginning of 2000, there were roughly 54 months where global crude was above 100 dollars a barrel. Of those 54 months, there was only 12 where global corn wasn't at least $6. When you have $100 crude, you have $6 corn—that's how the math has worked out historically.

real_qa.q: What percentage of U.S. farm net income came from government subsidies in 2025?
real_qa.r: In 2025, net farm income ended up at about $150 billion for crops and animal agriculture combined. Of that, somewhere between $80 to $90 billion was subsidies. So the whole thing is currently propped up by these government payments.

real_qa.q: How many acres of farmland nationwide are currently in Chapter 11 or Chapter 12 bankruptcy?
real_qa.r: There are 263,000 acres in Chapter 11 or Chapter 12 bankruptcy nationwide. In context, there are 27 million crop acres in Iowa alone, so the 263,000 acres is a rounding error.
real_qa.requete: farm bankruptcies Chapter 11 Chapter 12 acres nationwide

real_qa.q: What is the relationship between Iowa farmland returns and global oil price spikes over a 12-month period?
real_qa.r: If you own farmland in Iowa and want an above-average total return year, 12 months prior you wanted a global oil price spike. That connection and correlation is really tight—it's the tightest relative correlation when looking at all 50 states.
real_qa.requete: Iowa farmland returns oil price spike 12 months

real_qa.q: How much have mortgage interest rates increased relative to historical levels in Steve Bruere's 24-year career?
real_qa.r: Interest rates on mortgages were higher three weeks ago than at any point in his entire 24-year career. The cost of capital has gotten cheaper every year of his career until now, making it easy to look smart in farmland when capital was cheap.
real_qa.requete: mortgage interest rates 24 years career high

guest.bio_context: Steve Bruere has been working in farmland for 24 years and serves as President of People's Company. He has experienced the entire period where the cost of capital decreased every year of his career, giving him perspective on the current environment where interest rates have risen to levels higher than at any point in his entire career.
